correctness.rationale: The exact finite generator gives the j-subset moment recursion. The first three equations invert algebraically to severity q, normalized shock ratio and colonization share. A constructive rates argument proves sufficiency of the stated feasible domain, while a local one-parameter family proves failure of two-site identification. The Jacobian factorization is symbolic and strictly negative on its domain. CHECKER.py independently computes exact stationary probabilities from all finite configurations for N=3 and N=4, 216 rational parameter combinations, with 10,975 successful exact checks. No extrapolation from finite examples is needed for the proof.

evidence: Kapodistria, Phung-Duc and Resing 2015 formula (3.5) gives forward factorial moments; in finite patches j-wise occupancy equals normalized factorial moments, but no inverse theorem is asserted in inspected material. Its Section 5.3 and Lemma 5.2 additionally order the forward factorial moments by catastrophe severity while holding an effective removal rate fixed.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The local generator recursion has the same algebraic form as a forward moment system, and exchangeability converts moments to joint co-occurrence. This equivalence covers forward equations only, not global invertibility, minimal sufficient site count, feasibility, and inverse conditioning. No opposite reduction from the published statements giving those exact conclusions was identified. Lemma 5.2 is a genuine adjacent sensitivity comparison, but assumes demographic rates fixed and does not provide full joint inversion when local rates and shock rate are all unknown.

originality.rationale: The 2015 closely related full-text preprint already gives the forward factorial-moment product and a fixed-effective-rate factorial-moment ordering (Lemma 5.2, Section 5.3), openly acknowledged as prior. Its inspected model and formula sections do not state the inverse, three-site sharpness, exact attainable region, or conditioning Jacobian. Related 2004/2007 catastrophe literature and 2010 ecological occupancy inference were compared to the extent accessible. Published mathematical-result searches on multiple inverse-problem aliases did not identify a covering theorem. Unavailable earlier full texts and the ease of inverting the forward formula leave genuine historical-priority uncertainty.
residual_risks: The 2015 forward factorial-moment formula is mathematically close, making the inverse potentially implicit to specialists.

value.rationale: A mechanistically motivated ecological inverse problem asks whether common catastrophe frequency and per-event severity can be separated from static site occupancy. Exactly two sites fail generically while three succeed, yielding an explicit constructive feasible data domain and an exact ill-conditioning law. These are interpretable structural observability thresholds and falsifiable model restrictions, not routine arithmetic constants or unsupported downstream claims; they apply only to the stated homogeneous idealization.
